github_current_target_matches.title: Record reviewed partial bounds for vertical-fiber problem 10000043 (unresolved)
github_current_target_matches.body:
The vertical-fiber question remains unresolved. This package proves that infinite fiber intersections propagate across adjacent base vertices, and that when p_c(G)=1 an infinite cluster cannot have a uniform finite bound on its fiber intersections. The remaining case has finite intersections with every fiber but unbounded sizes across the base.

The source audit fixes the graph and bond-percolation conventions, credits the known bounded-cutset special case, and records why a stretched-tree example and an inhomogeneous ray block the attempted reductions. These examples do not refute the original question.

A separate adversarial AI review passed the frozen partial proof with no mandatory correction. The original 4,996 exact checks and 90,170 independent checks reproduce; the latter test interacting reservoirs, their independent base-edge law, full product-law completion, and a sharp 2M control. The written infinite-volume arguments were reviewed separately from these finite diagnostics. No novelty or human-peer-review claim is made.

All changed files are under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/10000043/. Queue status is unsolved and is maintained separately.
